title: Change a canister vacuum's dust bag: pull the full bag's collar up out of its holder, bin it, seat a new one
instruction: Put a new bag in the vacuum.
context: Changing the full dust bag in a bagged canister vacuum is one of the most familiar household chores (and routine for housekeeping staff). The bag's cardboard collar stands in a holder over the inlet: pulled up by its tab, the full bag comes out and goes in the bin without shedding dust; the new collar goes down the holder's channels square until it stops, so its gasket seals round the inlet; then the lid is shut and latched, while a hand steadies the vacuum, which rolls if pushed.
setup: Bench top is z = 0.7475 m; everything is real size. A bagged canister vacuum (470 mm long x 290 mm wide x 255 mm high, 5.5 kg: graphite ABS lower shell and rubber bumper, silver ABS upper shell and motor hood with a carry handle, two foot pedals, rear exhaust grille) stands free on its two 150 mm rear wheels and two front castors, front toward the arms, centred at y 0, front bumper at x 0.24 m; it rolls if pushed. Its dust compartment (175 x 250 mm inside, 20 mm side walls, floor 30 mm and rim 205 mm above the bench) is open: the red ABS domed lid (200 x 290 x 82 mm shell, 0.30 kg with its weight toward the latch at its front, inspection grille underneath) is swung back 100 degrees on its damped rear hinge at x 0.452 and rests on its stop. On the inside of the front wall a 38 mm inlet opens 130 mm above the bench, and over it stands the collar holder: two short upright grey plastic channels (12 mm gap, lips covering the collar's outer 4 mm for 30 mm up from the stop, chamfered lead-in at their tops and along the front wall's top edge) and a stop 70 mm above the bench. The full bag stands in it: a 120 x 125 x 2 mm printed cardboard collar with a 38 mm hole in a black rubber gasket ring and a 40 x 75 mm card grip tab on top, down on the stop, carrying a white quilted synthetic-fleece bag about two-thirds full of dust (127 x 200 x 117 mm; 0.18 kg in all). The vacuum's 38 mm corrugated black hose is plugged into the inlet socket on the front, curves down and lies along its right side to the handle behind it; the brushed-aluminium telescopic wand and the 240 mm floor nozzle lie across the bench behind it (x 0.785). To the front right an opened printed-paperboard carton of bags (140 x 75 x 75 mm, centred x 0.30, y -0.30) holds a new bag standing up in it: the same collar and tab with its folded fleece pack behind it (96 x 125 x 14 mm, 0.03 kg), its printed collar facing +y and its pack toward -y. To the front left stands an empty grey polypropylene wastebasket with a rolled rim (260 mm across, 230 mm tall) centred x 0.30, y 0.43. Real build: a bagged canister vacuum (e.g. Miele Complete C3 / Classic C1, which take GN bags) with its own bag holder taken out and the printed holder (fabrication/holder.stl, from vac.py's dimensions) taped to the compartment's front wall round the inlet; collar and gasket cut from fabrication/collar.svg; full bag made as in the README (150 g of wheat bran sealed in a quart freezer bag inside the fleece pouch, 180 g in all).
scoring: Positions are measured in the vacuum's frame where they concern the vacuum. 0.25: the old bag is out of the vacuum and its collar lies in the wastebasket (within its rim's radius less 10 mm, below the rim), no hand within 60 mm of its tab when let go, and it stays there. 0.5: and the new collar is started in the holder: its bottom edge inside the 12 mm channel (within 1 mm), centred across within 8 mm, square to the front wall within 10 degrees and below the channels' tops (100 mm above the bench). 0.75: and the new collar is seated, its bottom edge within 3 mm of the stop (above or below). 1.0: and the lid is shut on the rim and latched, every finger pad at least 80 mm from the latch and from the new collar's tab, and the vacuum, lid and new bag at rest (under 10 mm/s and 0.1 rad/s), held 1 s. The vacuum pushed more than 30 mm over the bench at any time caps the score at 0.5; either bag dropped on the bench (not in the bin, the carton or the vacuum) caps it at 0.25.
reset_notes: Fixed starting poses, no randomisation: vacuum square on its wheels, old bag seated in the holder, lid open on its stop and unlatched, new bag standing in its carton, wastebasket empty. The full bag is reusable: its bran stays sealed in the inner bag; refold it to 127 x 200 x 117 mm and re-seat it (about 2 minutes).
fidelity: PhysX 240 Hz. The vacuum is one free rigid body; its wheels are welded on and meet the bench with friction 0.15 (rolling resistance). The lid turns on a damped hinge, its weight toward its front; the latch is a rule: shut within 2 degrees and pressed within 60 mm of its button, the hinge is held by damping. Each bag is one rigid body (no sag, no dust); the collar is held only by the channels and stop. Hose and wand are drawn; motor and suction are not simulated.
